details.concept: Based on a detailed review of previous Gujarat Technological University (GTU) examination patterns and past paper question distributions for Object-Oriented Programming (OOP/OOPJ), the most frequently asked, high-weightage questions are structured below.
details.benefits: In GTU papers, theories are typically allocated 3 or 4 marks, while complete coding implementations or heavy conceptual programs carry a full 7 marks.

details.concept: These questions are asked in almost every paper.

1. Java Foundations & Core Concepts.1: What is Bytecode? Explain the architecture and key components of the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) in detail. (7 Marks) [link:1,t3]
1. Java Foundations & Core Concepts.2: List the prominent features of Java and explain any three. (3 or 4 Marks) [link:1,t2]
1. Java Foundations & Core Concepts.3: Differentiate between Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) and Procedure-Oriented Programming (POP). (3 or 4 Marks) [link:1,t9]

2. Classes, Objects, and Polymorphism.1: What is a Constructor? Differentiate between Parameterized and Copy Constructors with individual code examples. (7 Marks) [link:3,t5]
2. Classes, Objects, and Polymorphism.2: What is a static keyword? Explain its applications with variables, methods, and blocks along with a complete program. (7 Marks) [link:3,t10]
2. Classes, Objects, and Polymorphism.3: Explain Method Overloading vs. Method Overriding with syntax and code snippets. (7 Marks) [link:4.1,t8]
2. Classes, Objects, and Polymorphism.4: What is Run-Time Polymorphism? Explain Dynamic Method Dispatch with a clear, simple code example. (7 Marks) [link:4.1,t10]

3. Advanced OOP Structures & Exception H.1: Define an Interface. How does it structurally differ from an Abstract Class? Explain how multiple inheritance is achieved using interfaces. (7 Marks) [link:5.1,t7]
3. Advanced OOP Structures & Exception H.2: Explain the Exception Handling Mechanism in Java. Differentiate between Checked and Unchecked Exceptions. (4 or 7 Marks) [link:5.2,t3]
3. Advanced OOP Structures & Exception H.3: Explain the purpose and differences among the try, catch, finally, throw, and throws keywords. (4 or 7 Marks) [link:5.2,t2]

4. Concurrency & Utilities.1: Explain the life cycle of a Thread with a neat transition state diagram. (7 Marks) [link:6,t2]
4. Concurrency & Utilities.2: What is a Wrapper Class? Explain its significance along with the concepts of Autoboxing and Autounboxing. (4 or 7 Marks) [link:4.2,t2]

details.concept: GTU typically loops a set of standard, logical coding questions in Section 1(c) or 2(c). Expect these exact programs to show up (7 Marks):

Important Programs.1: Command-Line Arguments Program: Write a program to fetch 10 numbers from the command line and determine the maximum or minimum value. [link:0.1,p1]
Important Programs.2: Array Manipulation: Write a program to sort array elements in ascending order. [link:0.1,t2]
Important Programs.3: Mathematical Patterns: Programs to print the Fibonacci series up to n terms or find the sum of the individual digits of an entered number. [link:0.1,t3]
Important Programs.4: Custom Exceptions: Write a complete program that explicitly creates, raises, and handles a user-defined exception. [link:0.1,t4]
Important Programs.5: Text File I/O Handling: Write a program utilizing FileInputStream and FileOutputStream to dynamically read from and write text characters into a .txt file. [link:0.1,t5]

details.concept: Since JavaFX is standard for the GUI portion of modern syllabi, prepare these targeted concepts (Expected 4-7 Marks):

Key Questions.1: Explain the basic structure of a JavaFX application, highlighting the hierarchical roles of Stage, Scene, and the Scene Graph. (7 Marks) [link:8.1,t5]
Key Questions.2: List and briefly explain any four Layout Panes in JavaFX (specifically comparing GridPane, HBox, and VBox). (4 or 7 Marks) [link:8.1,t7]
Key Questions.3: Explain the entire lifecycle of a JavaFX Application (init(), start(), stop()). (4 Marks) [link:8.1,t4]
Key Questions.4: What is Property Binding in JavaFX? Explain with a simple code example. (4 Marks) [link:8.2,t2]

topics.title: Quick Strategy Tip for Your Exam

details.concept: When writing a GTU paper for OOP with Java, always write code snippets even if the question doesn't explicitly ask for a program. A 7-mark theory question on something like Dynamic Method Dispatch or Interfaces will automatically lose 2–3 marks if it lacks a supporting structural code demonstration!
details.Finally: Good luck with your semester 4 preparation!
